Context: This excerpt describes a city called Gold Hill in the Utah Territory in the western United States. In the `text(1850s)`, the discovery of silver brought people from many different places to the city. Most of the city’s leaders and politicians were immigrants from Europe. Miners were from China, Europe, and eastern states.
Title: Source 3: [Adapted from] “Gold-Rush Days: Virginia City, Nevada”
Author: by J. Ross Browne
Content: Gold Hill has grown into a city. Here the proof of hard work is clear. The whole hill is full of shafts and tunnels. Engine-houses for lifting are built on certain points. Quartz mills cover the sides of the canyon. The main street has many brick stores, hotels, the Pony Express office, and restaurants. It contains all those attractive places that go to make up a flourishing mining town. Even a newspaper is printed here.
